transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what brings you in to see me?

I came in because I’m worried about what’s been happening at work. I drive routes, and it feels like dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system. There are also these little comments over the radio that seem aimed at me.

People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell some of the other drivers are reporting on me. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or talking about you—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been longer than days or just a week. I’d say it’s felt clear to me for about two months now—the computer tracking and the comments over the radio.
Besides feeling that dispatch and other drivers are tracking or talking about you, have you ever actually heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard, like, voices when nobody’s there or anything like that. It’s more the things people say over the radio that feel directed at me.

Aside from these concerns about being tracked or talked about, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your job, keep up with your usual responsibilities, or interact with friends and family over the past two months?

Yeah… I have noticed changes. At work I’m falling behind on my route reports, and sometimes the instructions I give or follow get confusing enough that other drivers complain.

At home, my husband’s had to pick up a lot more. He’s been handling meals, phone calls, and basic planning because I’m just not keeping up like I usually would.

Before these clear feelings of being tracked and talked about started two months ago, did you notice any subtler changes—like feeling unusually suspicious, socially withdrawn, or just 'not quite yourself'—in the months leading up to that?

Yeah… looking back, it was building before the last two months. Probably around eight months total. It started after I got put in that temporary dispatch lead role, and I just didn’t feel quite right after that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persistent persecutory/referential delusions (belief that dispatch, computer systems, and coworkers are tracking and talking about her) lasting approximately 2 months in clear form, with a prodromal period of subtler suspiciousness extending the total duration to about 8 months. There is clear functional decline in both occupational (falling behind on reports, confusing instructions) and social/domestic domains (husband compensating for household responsibilities), meeting the impairment criterion. No hallucinations, disorganized speech, or mood episode symptoms were elicited, and the delusions are not bizarre but well-systematized around a real occupational context. The combination of a single, longstanding delusional theme plus prodromal decline and functional impairment exceeding 6 months supports a diagnosis of schizophrenia over delusional disorder (which would not typically feature such prominent functional and cognitive/behavioral disorganization) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (no mood symptoms reported).
